headline: Feed caught up and it's an ugly session: KSE-100 down as much as ~1,970 points intraday (to a low near 175,632) on fresh Middle East attacks, a global AI-stock sell-off, and surging oil prices — trading around 176,284 (-0.75%) at 1pm PKT, extending Tuesday's 638-point drop; drawdown from the Jan ATH now ~7.0%, still short of the 10% deploy-dry-powder line but the closest it's been in two weeks. AVN's sell-half plan is now two days overdue (flagged Jul 27, still unexecuted per holdings data) — place the order today, no further catalyst needed. EFERT's board met today (Jul 29) for H1 results/dividend but the outcome wasn't available in news searches as of review time — re-check next review.
market: A rough Wednesday: after Tuesday's 638-point pullback (KSE-100 closed 177,623.88 vs Monday's 178,262.34), today's session opened weak and deteriorated further — fresh attacks in the Middle East reignited US-Iran war jitters, sending oil prices sharply higher, while a broader Asian sell-off tied to AI-investment concerns weighed on regional sentiment too. The index fell as much as ~1,970 points intraday to a low around 175,632, and was quoted at 176,284.15 (-1,339.73 pts, -0.75%) as of 1:04pm PKT — selling was broad-based across auto assemblers, cement, chemicals, banks, E&P, OMCs and power generation. Against the Jan 23, 2026 all-time high of 189,556, that puts the drawdown at roughly 7.0-7.2% — worse than Monday/Tuesday's ~6%, but still clear of the 10% line that would trigger deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve. On the macro backdrop: S&P Global raised Pakistan's sovereign credit rating to 'B' from 'B-' this month, citing institutional stability and IMF-program reform progress — a supportive medium-term signal even as today's tape is ugly. Mali's price feed (data/prices.json) is current as of 11:50am PKT today, so per-holding figures below now reflect today's live tape rather than a lagged prior-day close. AVN's sell-half plan, flagged for eleven straight reviews now, was due two days ago (Mon Jul 27) — holdings data is still unchanged, suggesting it hasn't been executed; do it today regardless of today's broad-market wobble, there's no new negative AVN-specific catalyst driving today's dip, this is just the market-wide sell-off. EFERT's board met today (Jul 29, 9am) specifically to approve H1 2026 results and consider a dividend, per PSX's own announcement calendar — but the specific EPS/dividend figures weren't yet available in news/PSX searches at review time (results may still be getting formally disclosed or picked up by news outlets); treat the glut thesis (10-year-low H1 urea sales at 537K tons, 694K tons of inventory) as still the operative read until the actual print is confirmed at the next review. Note: the fund side of the price feed (ASSF, AKDISSF, NISIF, NISF, MIF, AICF, MICF, AKDISIF) has shown identical NAVs since Jul 24 — four straight trading sessions with no change, which looks more like a stalled MUFAP scrape than genuinely flat NAVs; flagged separately for a technical look, doesn't change today's investment calls. No confirmed ex-dividend dates within the next 3 days for any holding (MEBL's quarterly pattern suggests an August ex-date is plausible but wasn't confirmed in searches).
